subject: Post-call: ACME performance targets & draft SLA follow-up
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>, Sally Chen <sally.chen@acme.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-24T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call: ACME performance targets & draft SLA follow-up

Hi Alex / Sally —

Thanks again for the time this morning. Recap from our discovery and the performance points I committed to send over: 

Key performance asks you mentioned:
- Latency target: p95 <= 120ms for text generation (measured to first token) for interactive flows (concurrency ~8).
- Throughput: sustain ~500 requests/minute during peak periods with 2-3 second tail for batching bursts.
- Concurrency: ability to support 50 concurrent user sessions across the product (average 1-2 requests/sec per session).
- Streaming: partial-token streaming required for the chat UI; first partial token should start streaming within 150ms of model first-token boundary when possible.
- Availability: target 99.5% platform availability for the dedicated pool.

Next steps I suggested:
1) I’ll share a draft SLA language that codifies latency measurement method, exclusions, reporting cadence, and remedies.
2) We’ll run a short perf validation/proof-of-performance during sandbox week (TBD) to validate p95 under your concurrency pattern.
3) Procurement: send initial commercial terms and a draft SOW to procurement.

I’ve attached a first-pass SLA draft that mirrors what we discussed (ACME-Redwood-SLA-draft-v1.pdf). Please review and call out anything that doesn’t match your expectation around measurement or remedies.

Thanks —
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0199

Attachment: ACME-Redwood-SLA-draft-v1.pdf (PDF, 12 pages)

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Sally Chen <sally.chen@acme.com>
Cc: procurement@acme.com
Date: 2026-06-24T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: ACME performance targets & draft SLA follow-up

Marissa — thanks for the clear recap and the SLA draft. A couple of clarifying questions before we loop legal/procurement: 

1) Latency measurement: when you say "measured to first token", can you clarify the ingress point? Are you measuring from our client-side request time, from the HTTP accept time at your gateway, or from when the model actually generates the token? We need reproducible measurement for our telemetry.

2) Exclusions: we assume scheduled maintenance, third-party outages, and customer network issues are excluded from SLO calculations. Any additional exclusions we should expect? What about model fallback events (e.g., an automatic downgrade to a smaller variant when capacity constrained)?

3) Reporting cadence: we want weekly slice reports during ramp and a monthly SLA reconciliation. Is that supported?

4) Remedies: the draft mentions credits — can you outline the proposed credit tiers (e.g., p95 miss frequency -> percentage)? We’ll want something that scales with severity.

Finally, for streaming: can you confirm you support chunked partial tokens and what the behavior is under high concurrency (do partials get buffered)? We want to ensure our chat UI won’t appear blocked during bursts.

If we can get these clarified I’ll push to procurement/legal and ask for a redline.

—Alex
Alex Johnson, Senior Product Manager | Acme Robotics
alex.johnson@acme.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>, Sally Chen <sally.chen@acme.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-24T13:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: ACME performance targets & draft SLA follow-up

Alex — great questions. Short answers then a few specifics below.

- Measurement point: we measure latency at Redwood ingress (the time the request is accepted by our API gateway) to the timestamp of the first byte of model-generated content returned to the client. We can provide a measurement spec (HTTP header markers and trace IDs) so you can align your telemetry.

- Exclusions: agreed on scheduled maintenance, third-party provider outages, and customer network issues. Additional exclusions we include: first request cold start for a model variant (first 5 requests after an idle period >30 min per worker), and any customer-configured model fallback events triggered by policy (we record fallback occurrences separately).

- Streaming behavior: we support chunked/partial-token streaming. Under high concurrency we prioritize low-latency preemption to deliver first partials; we do not batch partials into larger payloads more than 30ms beyond token production in normal operation. In extreme overload we may buffer up to 200ms as part of backpressure; those scenarios would be visible as degraded SLO and covered under remedies.

- Reporting cadence / remedies: we publish weekly SLO dashboards for customers during ramp and maintain a monthly reconciliation report. For remedies we propose tiered service credits: 0.5-1.0% credit for minor p95 misses, up to 5% credit for sustained or severe breaches — the draft SLA has a table (page 6) with proposed percentages and thresholds.

I’ve attached the SLA again and highlighted the measurement/exclusion bits on page 3-7. If ok, I’ll ask our legal to prepare a DocuSign-ready version and loop procurement. Otherwise, call out any redlines you want us to address first.

Thanks —
Marissa

Attachment: ACME-Redwood-SLA-draft-v1.pdf (highlighted pages 3-7)

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-24T15:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: ACME performance targets & draft SLA follow-up

Looping in briefly — thanks for driving this, Marissa. A few internal notes for ACME:
- Remedies: Laura/legal will propose final credit bands; from Sales we prefer an approach that ties credits to monthly reconciliation (so credits scale with spend).
- Availability target: 99.5% for the dedicated pool is reasonable; we should confirm scope (control plane vs data plane).
- Action: Marissa/Laura to set up a 30-min call with ACME legal next week to walk the SLA and redlines.

Marissa — can you add the meeting invite once Alex confirms availability?

Thanks,
Rishi
VP, Sales | Redwood Inference

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>

Cc: Sally Chen <sally.chen@acme.com>, procurement@acme.com
Date: 2026-06-25T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: ACME performance targets & draft SLA follow-up

Thanks Marissa / Rishi — this is helpful. Please go ahead and send the DocuSign-ready SLA; procurement will expect a doc they can redline. I can be available for a legal walkthrough next Tuesday (6/30) from 10–11am PT.

One last ask: include an explicit clause that describes how network-level retries from our client are treated for latency measurement (i.e., do retries get treated as separate requests or are they correlated). That will help our telemetry folks.

If you send the updated doc and a calendar invite for 6/30, we’ll move this to procurement review.

—Alex
